text:
Separating punishment from its justification keeps analysis clear: we can identify the practice—deliberately imposing hardship for an offense—without assuming any contested rationale like retribution or deterrence is essential to it. Conflating them can make one justification seem built into punishment itself, obscuring alternatives and biasing debates about when punishment is permissible. This matters because punishment as a social institution operates independently of the moral reasons offered for it.
